calls.beyond: Carolina has a better power play than most, and Vancouver has one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a big night: Carolina’s power play created 21.0 expected goals per 60, against their usual 8.2 (about 8.9 against Vancouver) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 150 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina an 82% chance, and they delivered.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver only an 18% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Carolina picked Vancouver’s defense apart
surprises.body: Vancouver usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: Carolina’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.6% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (about 6.8% against Vancouver) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Stankoven’s hat trick, one at every strength
paras: K'Andre Miller got the scoring started for the Hurricanes a little over a minute in. Andrei Svechnikov scored midway through the first and again a little over two minutes later on the power play to stretch the lead to 3-0. It was a busy second period. Mark Jankowski made it 4-0 early in the period, but Jake DeBrusk got the Canucks on the board 43 seconds later. Logan Stankoven stretched the lead to 5-1 shorthanded midway through the period, and he scored again on the power play late in the period to make it 6-1. Vancouver pulled Kevin Lankinen after six goals and turned to Leevi Meriläinen to start the third. Stankoven completed a natural hat trick midway through the third to make it 7-1 for the Hurricanes. DeBrusk struck again a minute and a half later to cut Carolina’s lead to 7-2, far too late to matter. Stankoven’s goals came one shorthanded, one on the power play and one at even strength. Sean Walker assisted on all three, and had four assists in all.

The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Hurricanes win about seven in ten. Pyotr Kochetkov made 18 saves for the Canes. By our Swing measure, Shayne Gostisbehere had the best night of anyone, even with Stankoven’s hat trick in the game.
The Hurricanes went 3-for-3 on the power play. The Hurricanes killed all four Canucks power plays. The Hurricanes moved to 3-1-1, and the Canucks dropped to 2-3-0.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Hurricanes.
Elias Pettersson (#40) has a point in every game this season.
Nikolaj Ehlers’s five-game point streak against Vancouver ended.
The Hurricanes have beaten the Canucks five straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
